New: A new top rarity: Aetheric, above Zenith, with every effect of the rarities below it plus a turning halo of light. Wild Aetheric Aetherlings live only on Zenith Spire, and two Zeniths can rarely breed one with the finest materials.
Overseer Vance has a new final goal: own an Aetheric Aetherling.
Balancing: Expeditions

Each island brings one new rarity: Whisperleaf Hollow has only Dims, Fractured Quarry adds Faint, Smoldering Caldera adds Steady, and so on up to Zenith in Stormsea Expanse and Aetheric atop Zenith Spire.
Expeditions
Fractured Quarry's wild Aetherlings are a little stronger and Zenith Spire's a little weaker, to keep each island as hard as before.
Expeditions
Wild Aetherlings rarer than Dim turn up less often on every island. A Gleaming can now appear in Whisperleaf Hollow, as a very rare find.
Expeditions
Rarity makes an Aetherling attack a little faster instead of a lot faster, so levels count for more in a fight. Every island's waves and boss were rebalanced to match.
Expeditions
Old Thicketroll is weaker: a party of Dims at level 7 can now beat him.
Nexus
Caught and hatched Aetherlings have traits less often, and strong traits are rarer.
Breeding
Eggs jump past their expected rarity less often.
Market
The Glimmer Lure now makes rarer wild Aetherlings 50% more common, down from twice as common.

New: Gravelnip and Wraithwire are painted in their final form: every Aetherling now has art for all three forms.

Balancing: Aether-Log
Catching a later form no longer counts its earlier forms as found: each form is found on its own.
Expeditions
Auto-bind now tries every form you haven't had yet, and counts copies per form.

New: 14 more Aetherlings are painted in their final form, including Boltkit's three flame tails and Gridrift's orbiting star cage. Only two are left to paint.

Bugfixes: The owned mark on wild Aetherlings and on an island's list now means you have had that exact form: catching a later form no longer marks its first form.

QOL: The close button on windows is bigger and flatter, with no ring behind it.

New: The close button on every window is newly painted in violet to match the rest of the interface.
Brambletide, Drizzlenub and Murkroot are painted in their final form.

Balancing: Expeditions

Experience from each defeated enemy is now shared evenly by the party members still standing. Each enemy gives three times as much, so a full party levels as fast as before, and a smaller party gets bigger shares.

New: Windows close with a round ✕ button.
A species' page names all three forms under their pictures and is headed by the chosen form's name; Creaturedex cards are named for the form they show.
Bugfixes: Tooltips open clear of the mouse pointer, so they no longer catch your clicks.

New: 13 more hybrid and secret-recipe Aetherlings are painted in their final form, from Burrbolt's storm tail to Murkmire's abyss bloom.
On first launch the window fits your screen, and the text starts larger when the window is smaller than 1920×1080.
If your save can't be read and an older copy is loaded instead, the game now tells you.
Bugfixes: No more stutter on every capture or level-up with hundreds of Aetherlings: only the cards that changed are redrawn.
Creaturedex portraits scrolled out of view no longer animate in the background.
The Form 2 and Form 3 buttons no longer reveal the shapes of species you have never seen.

New: The Creaturedex can show every card as Form 1, 2 or 3, at the highest rarity you have owned with its effects, and in shiny colours once you have caught a shiny.
A species' page shows one form at a time: a large portrait with the three forms as thumbnails, and its description and facts at full width beside it.

title: Hybrids and secret recipes get their pictures

New: All 45 hybrid and secret-recipe Aetherlings are painted in their first two forms, and 13 of them in their final form too.
111 item icons are newly painted: ores, bars, logs, herbs, fish, meals, threads, parts and vessels.
Patch notes on the title screen: every version's changes, sorted by kind.
Sound effects have their own switches: rare finds, notifications, battle and interface sounds.
Click an item to see where it comes from: skills, rare finds, each island's drop chance, bosses and the Market.
The Sanctum tab shows a gold "claim!" chip when Overseer Vance's goal is done, and its tooltip names the goal.
QOL: Tooltips on the Genesis Pods and Expeditions tabs say how many eggs are ready and which shinies wait for a vessel.
The item panel scrolls, so long lists fit.
Rarity pips and the sparkles on portraits and frames have smooth edges.
On screens 1440 px wide or smaller, a new game starts with the Interface scale at 115%.

Bugfixes: Icons and sprites were drawn with hard, stair-stepped edges; they are smooth again.
Portraits, orbit dots, Aether-Log dots and battle shadows are drawn anti-aliased.
The Repeat switch's text was cut off at the new sizes.
QOL: Rounder corners on pills and boxes.
The game is laid out at 1920x1080, so the most common screen draws 1:1 with no stretching: sharper text and icons at the same size as before.
Every Market tab gives all its cards one size, so a locked card is as big as an open one.
Bugfixes: Fixed an error when leaving the Nexus while its list was scrolling.
A copy is kept from the start of each session and before every import; imports are checked first.
Thorns that knock out an attacker are handled correctly.
Keeps your page and a stable order when the list changes.
Bulk release's "Release shinies too" and "Release working ones too" showed as bare text; they are real switches now.
QOL: Bulk release filters and switches sit on inset cards, like the Options pages.

New: Wild Aetherlings roll their form: Form 2 from level 20, Form 3 from level 40. One caught below its level's form evolves as it levels.
Bulk release by rarity range, type, species and level, keep the best few of each species, with a live preview.
Every sidebar tab has a key you can change (Options > Controls), shown as a keycap on the tab.
Item tooltips and tiles say what an item is used for; sell treasure from the Inventory.
Sprites breathe, sway and hop now and then while idle.
Fill empty slots on a skill page in one click.
QOL: XP from every kill shows at once, with live XP bars and a level-up pop.
The log says the chance each bind or escape had.
The island list and log fold away; the panel under the battle keeps one height.
Filters on one row of dropdowns and a tidier detail panel.
The Put to work menu's skill icons are drawn at text size.
Pickers still show what an Aetherling is doing under a card's note.
Styled tooltip cards; mouse back and forward buttons change page.
Speeding up a whole hatch costs about what the egg did.
Attune: a lock costs by the trait's strength; Lock pills instead of switches.
Bugfixes: A closing dialog no longer eats the next click; changing page closes a page's dialogs.
Clicks could be lost while a screen was updating.
Works Build buttons follow your gold live and their clicks aren't lost.
The goal card now shows Claim for item and counter goals.
The window no longer unmaximizes on its own.
Thousands of Aetherlings no longer slow the game to a crawl.
Balancing: Expeditions
Bosses from island 5 on were pushovers; every island now has one wave margin and a boss a little tougher than its waves.
Cooking
The first three islands drop fish, so meals exist before the first Aqueous Aetherling.

New: A new title screen with three save slots, a full Options menu and progress while you're away.
A full Market: stock, rotating offers, boosts, extra work slots, bulk selling and the Egg Market.
Aether Pearls: an endgame currency with six Pearl upgrades in Sanctum Works.
Overseer Vance has 112 goals paced over the month (was 26).
Four late islands (levels 59 to 95) with painted battle backdrops.
Ten material tiers per skill, ten egg tiers and ten vessel tiers.
Rarity pips, animated top-tier colours, shiny nameplates and rarity effects on sprites and frames.
Shiny and rare entrance effects, type attack sounds, and damage numbers that spread out.
A boss track, looping music and a sound of its own for evolution.
QOL: Work slots: up to ten per skill.
The worker picker lists each Aetherling's trait bonuses and sorts by best output or secondary.
Action cards show how many of the product, rare drop and treasure you have.
An Owned badge on island previews and wild fighters.
Auto-bind chances as pills in each rarity's colour.
No faint grey numbers: counts, levels and stats are coloured chips.
Bugfixes: The Options panel went blank after going fullscreen.
The detail panel could be pushed off screen.
Fighters faced the wrong way; the Sanctum expedition card didn't update.
Saves are written safely, so a crash mid-save can't break one.
Balancing: Breeding
Inherited traits never come out weaker than the parent's; shiny parents raise an egg's shiny chance a little.
Breeding
Breeding odds follow the parents' rarity.
Expeditions
Levels matter in a fight; the first boss and Fractured Quarry are tougher.
Game
Skill and Aetherling levelling paced so every skill reaches 99 in about a month; Aetherlings level up to 100.
Market
Sell prices sit below shop prices; crafted goods are worth more than their inputs.
